email.body1:
Justin, saw Bitsight crossed $200M ARR and was named a Leader in the Q2 2026 Forrester Wave after folding in Cybersixgill.

Growth and an acquisition together flood the funnel with signals faster than they can be turned into action. Our AI SDR closes that signal-to-action latency, researching, writing, and following up autonomously: 3-5x more meetings per rep, no new hires.

I built a personalized signal play for Bitsight off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Justin, quick follow-up for Bitsight.

Integrating Cybersixgill usually means messy data and cross-sell signals stacking up faster than reps can act. As RevOps, you feel that latency first, and it's hard to show measurable lift while systems are still merging.

Want 15 minutes? I'll walk you through a teardown of your current outbound, three things I'd change. Our best practices alone usually lift response rates 50 to 70 percent.
email.body3:
Justin, last bit of proof for Bitsight.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Bitsight's reply rate likely compares to other cybersecurity software teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Justin, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If tightening signal-to-action without adding headcount isn't a priority while Cybersixgill integrates, no problem at all. A milestone and a merger at once is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a RevOps motion? I'll tailor it to Bitsight either way.
